newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index up on rise in foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index up on rise in foreign demand.

text.p: Increased foreign demand at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Monday helped the NSE'S 20-share index to gain 13.31 points to close at 3548.31, dealers said.
Turnover was posted at 29.252 million shillings on 480,896 shares from Friday's 11.664 million shillings on 269,686 shares.

Foreign investors bought 50,800 shares of Uchumi Supermarket at 40 from 58, 15,700 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 87 and 89 from 87 and 35,000 shares of Firestone East Africa at 30 unchanged.
Uchumi Supermarket traded at 40 ex-bonus but brokers said they expected the price to go higher on foreign demand.
Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting closed 15 up at 280 from 265. Last week the share shed 74.

"There was a lot of underselling last week which brought the price down, but I think there was a rush for it since it might start trading ex-all on Friday this week," a broker said. "But nobody knows yet for sure."
The company issued a dividend of 8 and a bonus issue of two shares for every one held. The bonus issue awaits approval from the Capital Markets Authority.
On average, prices on key shares were firm. Barclays Bank closed at 108 from 105, while Standard Chartered Bank gained 2.50 to close at 53.
Sasini Tea & Coffee traded at 75 unchanged while Kenya Airways closed at 9.80 from 9.70.
